C131.label: yellow_key_directly_in_front
C131.evidence: In all ON images, the yellow key is located exactly one cell straight ahead of the agent, whereas in all OFF images, the key is located elsewhere, carried by the agent, or missing entirely.
C131.raw:
Step 1:
ON example 1: A yellow key is exactly one cell in front of the agent, and a yellow door is two cells forward and one cell to the right.
ON example 2: A yellow key is exactly one cell in front of the agent, and a yellow door is one cell forward and one cell to the left.
ON example 3: A yellow key is exactly one cell in front of the agent, and a yellow door is one cell forward and one cell to the right.
ON example 4: A yellow key is exactly one cell in front of the agent, and a yellow door is directly to the right of the agent.
ON example 5: A yellow key is exactly one cell in front of the agent, and a yellow door is one cell forward and one cell to the right.
ON example 6: A yellow key is exactly one cell in front of the agent, and a yellow door is directly to the left of the agent.
ON example 7: A yellow key is exactly one cell in front of the agent, and a yellow door is one cell forward and one cell to the left.
ON example 8: A yellow key is exactly one cell in front of the agent, and a yellow door is two cells forward and one cell to the right.
OFF example 1: A yellow key is directly to the left of the agent, and a yellow door is two cells straight ahead.
OFF example 2: A yellow key is directly to the right of the agent, and a yellow door is two cells forward and two cells to the right.
OFF example 3: A yellow door is one cell forward and one cell to the left, and no key is visible.
OFF example 4: A yellow key is one cell forward and one cell to the left, and a yellow door is directly to the right of the agent.
OFF example 5: The agent is carrying the yellow key (it is in the agent's cell), and a yellow door is one cell forward and one cell to the right.
OFF example 6: A yellow key is directly to the right of the agent, and a yellow door is one cell forward and one cell to the left.
OFF example 7: A yellow key is two cells left of the agent, and a yellow door is two cells forward and one cell to the left.
OFF example 8: A yellow key is one cell forward and one cell to the right, and a yellow door is two cells forward and one cell to the right.

Step 2:
The distinguishing property is the position of the yellow key relative to the agent. In every ON image, the yellow key is located exactly one square directly in front of the agent. In the OFF images, the yellow key is found in other positions (to the side, diagonally forward, multiple squares away), being carried by the agent, or not visible at all.
